front: Import vs DirectQuery vs Direct Lake
back: Import caches a compressed copy — fastest, needs refresh. DirectQuery queries the source every interaction — always current, slower, limited DAX. Direct Lake reads Delta tables in OneLake with import speed and no refresh. Keyword: storage mode.
Mixes storage modes across tables so a huge fact table stays DirectQuery while small dimensions are imported. Keyword: per-table mode.
Classify each source as Public, Organizational, or Private. Power Query refuses to fold a query that would leak data from a Private source, which appears as a refresh failure. Keyword: refresh error.
Reserved date/time parameter names that must filter the fact table for incremental refresh to be configurable. Keyword: incremental refresh.
Reference starts from the original's output, so upstream changes flow down. Duplicate copies every step into an independent query. Keyword: linked vs independent.
Turn it off for staging queries used only as a source for others, so they do not appear as tables in the model. Keyword: staging query.
Distribution shows distinct and unique counts — how you prove a key is unique. Profile gives full statistics for one column. Both default to the top 1000 rows. Keyword: 1000-row default.
Remove errors deletes the failing rows. Replace errors substitutes a value and keeps them — usually right for a numeric column that should read zero. Keyword: keep the row?
Propagates the last non-null value downward. The standard fix for a source that prints a category only on its first row. Keyword: sparse source.
Turns value-columns into attribute/value rows and keeps working when a new column appears next period. The transformation that makes a spreadsheet into a fact table. Keyword: resilient.
Append stacks rows from same-shaped tables. Merge joins columns from another query on a key. Rows versus columns. Keyword: which axis.
Left anti returns rows with no match in the second table — the tool for finding fact rows whose dimension key is missing before you build the relationship. Keyword: unmatched.
Narrow fact tables of measurements and keys, wide dimension tables of attributes, one row per thing. The shape Power BI's engine is built for. Keyword: fact and dimension.
Single — filters flow from the one side to the many side. Both directions invites ambiguity errors; prefer CROSSFILTER inside the one measure that needs it. Keyword: single.
Activates an inactive relationship for one calculation. How a single date table serves order date, ship date, and due date. Keyword: role-playing dimension.
One row per date, no gaps, full years, a date-typed key, and marked as a date table. Without it, time intelligence returns wrong answers rather than errors. Keyword: silently wrong.
It creates a hidden date table per date column, inflating model size and refresh, and ignores fiscal calendars. Use one explicit date table. Keyword: hidden tables.
A column is computed at refresh, stored, and sliceable. A measure is computed at query time in filter context and stores nothing. Aggregations belong in measures. Keyword: when evaluated.
Evaluates an expression with modified filter context, replacing any existing filter on the same column. Wrap the condition in KEEPFILTERS to add instead of replace. Keyword: filter context.
Remove filters to build a denominator. ALL clears everything, ALLEXCEPT keeps the named columns, ALLSELECTED respects what the user picked outside the visual. Keyword: percent of total.
Evaluate an expression row by row over a table then aggregate — needed when the calculation is not on an existing column, such as quantity times price. Keyword: row by row.
Sums across most dimensions but not time — stock levels, account balances. Built with LASTDATE, FIRSTNONBLANK, or CLOSINGBALANCEMONTH. Keyword: not over time.
One set of calculation items (YTD, prior year, variance) written once with SELECTEDMEASURE and applied to any measure, instead of writing variants of each. Keyword: SELECTEDMEASURE.
Remove high-cardinality columns. Splitting datetime into date and time, or dropping an unused GUID, beats deleting rows because compression is per column. Keyword: cardinality.
Records each visual's duration split into DAX query, visual display, and other, and exports the DAX. Slow DAX is a model problem; slow display means too many data points. Keyword: which phase.
Makes month names sort in calendar order using a numeric column. The sort column must share the display column's granularity or the setting is rejected. Keyword: same granularity.
Bar for magnitude across categories, line for change over time, scatter for the relationship between two measures, matrix when the reader needs an exact value. Keyword: what comparison.
A JSON file setting palette, fonts, and default visual formatting report-wide, overridable per visual. Keyword: apply once.
Drives colour from a DAX measure returning a hex code — the escape hatch when the rule is too complex for a scale or a threshold. Keyword: measure returns colour.
DAX computed on the visual's own result set, so running totals and rank-within-the-visual need no model change. Keyword: on the visual.
Visual, page, report, and all-pages. Slicers are filters rendered on the canvas for readers to drive. Keyword: scope.
Sets what selecting a point in one visual does to the others — filter, highlight, or nothing. Keyword: cross-filter behaviour.
If Data is checked the bookmark overrides the reader's slicer choices. Uncheck it to switch only what is displayed. Keyword: what it captures.
A report page sized to the Tooltip preset with its Tooltip toggle on, then referenced from a visual's Tooltip formatting. Keyword: page as tooltip.
A target page declares a drillthrough field; readers right-click a data point anywhere to jump there filtered to that value. A back button is added automatically. Keyword: right-click.
A separate portrait canvas. Visuals not placed on it do not appear on a phone at all. Keyword: opt-in per visual.
Set in the Selection pane, this is what keyboard and screen-reader users follow — accessibility is configured here, not just in alt text. Keyword: Selection pane.
Grouping combines chosen categorical values; binning buckets a numeric or date range; clustering finds natural groups across several fields. Keyword: which input.
Key influencers ranks what drives a metric up or down. The decomposition tree lets a reader break a measure down field by field interactively. Keyword: explain vs explore.

front: When to use a paginated report
back: Pixel-perfect printing or PDF — invoices, regulatory returns, long tables with repeating headers. Built in Power BI Report Builder as RDL. Keyword: printable document.
Viewer reads. Contributor creates and edits. Member also publishes and updates the app and shares. Admin also deletes the workspace and manages Admins. Keyword: publish needs Member.
It is personal, cannot be shared by role, and its content disappears with the account. Shared content belongs in a real workspace. Keyword: not collaboration.
The workspace is where authors work; the app is the packaged read-only view for consumers, with its own navigation and audiences. Keyword: audience.

front: Consumers still see the old report
back: The app was not updated. Changes in the workspace are invisible to app users until you publish the update. Keyword: update app.
Public to the entire internet with no authentication. Never the answer for confidential data, and usually disabled by the tenant admin. Keyword: anonymous.
Eight scheduled refreshes a day on shared capacity, up to 48 on Premium or Fabric capacity. Keyword: capacity.
Whenever the service must reach a source that is not accessible from the cloud — on-premises or inside a private network. Cloud sources need none. Keyword: reachability.
Standard is shared, centrally managed, and supports scheduled refresh, DirectQuery, and live connections. Personal is single-user and Import refresh only. Keyword: production.
An alert fires when a dashboard card, gauge, or KPI crosses a threshold. A subscription emails a rendered snapshot on a schedule. Keyword: threshold vs schedule.
The role was created in Desktop but no members were added to it in the service. Both steps are required. Keyword: assign members.
One role using USERPRINCIPALNAME against a permissions table, instead of one hardcoded role per region. Keyword: USERPRINCIPALNAME.
Promoted is applied by anyone with write access. Certified is restricted to reviewers the tenant admin authorises and ranks higher in discovery. Neither changes permissions. Keyword: endorsement.
